chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about two men who had shared property, part of which was debt and part was specific assets. They divided the specific assets and the debt. The share of one of them from the debt was paid off or partially paid off, and the share of the other remained. I asked: Does he return [the value] to his partner? He said: 'Yes, as long as it does not consume his capital.'
ai.seo_question: How is debt and asset division handled in Islamic partnership when one partner's debt is paid off?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the equitable distribution of mixed partnership assets where one share is a debt (dayn) and the other is tangible property (ayn). The ruling establishes that if one partner's portion of the debt is settled, the other partner is entitled to compensation from the remaining assets, ensuring that the value of the first partner's share is preserved. This principle underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in commercial partnerships, preventing unjust enrichment when assets are liquidated or divided.
